publication_status.evidence: Crossref API (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1051/0004-6361/202453248) returns A&A volume 694, issued 2025-02 for this title; DOI redirects (302) to https://www.aanda.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202453248 (publisher returned 403 to curl). arXiv 2501.04103 has no journal_ref field, only 'Accepted to A&A'. Article number A208 is from the task statement, not verified in Crossref (article-number field empty). Values below are from the arXiv v1 PDF, which is the A&A proof ('aa53248-24corr'); the final published version might differ.

method: PMOIRED geometrical model fit to 12 GRAVITY (high resolution, K band) snapshots, using a 16 nm region around Br-gamma, fitting normalized line profile, T3PHI, DPHI and |V| simultaneously. Model: two uniform disks (both fixed at 0.15 mas) plus a Keplerian disk at the Be star position (contributes only in the line). Free: v_orb sin i_disk, RV_Be, dRA, dDec, f_pre-sd, FWHM_disk, i_disk, PA_disk, EW. Orbits fitted to the 12 positions with IDL orbfit-lib (Newton-Raphson); combined solution adds FEROS RVs from Gies & Wang 2020. No priors stated beyond fixed parameters (Sect. 3.1, p. 3; Sect. 4.1, p. 4).
flux_ratio_definition: f_pre-sd 'parameterized as the contribution of the pre-sd star to the total continuum flux' (Sect. 3.1, p. 3); Table A.1 column f_pre-sd,tot 'total flux fraction of the pre-sd star'. K-band, around Br-gamma (2.166 um), normalized so Be star + disk + pre-sd sum to 1 in the continuum. Weighted mean f_pre-sd = 0.439 +/- 0.013 (p. 4). The conventional contrast pre-sd/Be would be f/(1-f) (about 0.78), but that is NOT stated in the paper; derived by caller if needed.
uncertainties: Per-epoch errors from PMOIRED bootstrapping; 'the errors do not include contributions from possible systematics such as small-scale miscalibration of the data due to rapidly changing atmospheric conditions during observations' (Sect. 3.1, p. 4). So statistical only. Astrometric orbit residuals rms 19-25 uas (Table 3). RV errors have an added 12 km/s (21 km/s for 2021 Sep 05) wavelength-calibration term, but that affects only the GRAVITY RVs, not the astrometry.

conventions.PA: north to east (Table A.1 notes, p. 11); dRA, dDec = pre-sd star relative to the Be star (Be star treated as primary), east and north
conventions.omega: omega_pre-sd in the astrometric-only fits (Table 2); omega_Be in the combined fits (Table 3). Table 3 note: 'longitude of the periastron (fixed at 90 deg for circular orbits)'. Hence omega_Be=111.9 and omega_pre-sd would differ by 180 deg in the usual convention, but Table 2 omega_pre-sd=117.6 (astrometry only) is close to Table 3 omega_Be=111.9, so the paper's labelling is not self-evidently consistent; check before use. The paper does not state which star's orbit the relative astrometry follows beyond 'companion relative to primary'.
conventions.Omega: 'longitude of the ascending node'; 'position angle of the line of nodes' (Sect. 4.1, p. 5). Not stated whether the ascending node is the receding one; Omega=25 deg is close to PA_disk (27.9+/-5.5 deg), which the paper says should be parallel to the line of nodes.
conventions.other: T0 = epoch of periastron (eccentric) or of superior conjunction (circular), in RJD = JD-2400000 (Table 2 note). q = M_pre-sd/M_Be. Primary = Be star. Distance 296.0+/-8.0 pc from dynamical parallax.

orbit.headline: eccentric, astro + RVs (both stars) solution, the one quoted in the abstract (e, a, d, M_Be)
T_peri_mjd: converted from the paper's T0 = 53220.6 RJD (RJD = JD-2400000 = MJD+0.5)

masses.note: Table 3 prints 0.270+/-0.027 for eccentric astro+RVs but 0.270+/-0.056 for eccentric astro+RV_pre-sd+K_Be; the abstract quotes 0.270+/-0.056 alongside the astro+RVs values for e, a. 0.027 is consistent with q and M_Be error propagation (0.270*sqrt((0.0044/0.0638)^2+(0.31/4.24)^2)=0.027). Possible inconsistency in the paper.

notes: Table A.1 gives positions without rho/PA errors (error ellipses only); rho and PA are the measured PMOIRED positions (not posterior predictions). All 12 positions used in all orbit fits (the three 3-sigma outliers were tested by exclusion with parameters staying within 1 sigma). Headline per abstract: eccentric astro+RVs. Per-epoch disk values are in Table A.2 (p. 11), not transcribed here. Table A.2 header says v_orb sin i in [mas], clearly a typo for km/s. Mean disk inclination is ~2 sigma below orbital i; paper judges the difference not significant. MJD column here = HJD_mean - 2400000.5 (derived by me; paper lists HJD-2400000). The paper does not state a dRA/dDec to rho/PA consistency check; rho and PA are as printed.
